summary: The pairing the audience had been demanding in other episodes' comments, and the payoff shows in the ratio: 3,947 comments on 879K views, the highest comment-per-view rate in the entire corpus. The top comment, with over 5,000 likes, is a fan playfully scolding her idol for not being able to hold eye contact. Others note she was too shy to look at him at all, and immediately escalate the request to a duet. One comment marks the moment as the pairing finally becoming real. The channel's pinned comment asks who should come next, continuing the queue.

audience_signals: The highest comment-per-view rate in the corpus — roughly 0.45%, about seven times the long-form talk average — and it came from booking exactly the pair the comments had been asking for
Delivering a requested booking does not end the demand; it converts into the next ask, here a duet, so the format compounds
Idol fandoms deliver disproportionate comment volume relative to views, which means this series is undervalued if judged on views alone
Shyness and restraint generate more engagement than confidence in this format — the tension is the product
content_requests: A duet between the two guests
Keep taking pairing requests from the comments
